text:
alex_support: Heads-up — ACME reporting a batch of streaming requests flagged as 5xx. Customer says client closed the socket mid-stream, but our billing shows 5xx. Sample trace and curl repro incoming. Can someone triage? :eyes:

customer_acme: Repro steps — simple streaming request, then client app calls close() after ~300ms. We see logs showing error on the gateway and tokens billed as failed. curl snippet:```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d $PROMPT\n# client then kills process after first chunk\n```
Logs:```
[2026-03-10T17:12:34Z] upstream write error: write tcp 10.0.0.5:443->10.2.3.4:56342: broken pipe
[2026-03-10T17:12:34Z] classify_response: marked 5xx due to write error
```

maya_oncall: Thanks — looking at metrics now. I see a spike in gateway.write_err and eof_classified_5xx at 17:12:30Z. Request IDs?

customer_acme: IDs: r_7a1b2c, r_7a1b3d, r_7a1b4f. Happens across languages (node/python). Not reproducible every time but ~3% of streams.

jordan_infra: Pushed trace for r_7a1b2c. The proxy stack returns EPIPE on write after client FIN. Our current pipeline treats upstream write failures as 5xx. We probably need to differentiate client-initiated FIN vs upstream error.

alex_support: Is there a reliable fingerprint to tell FIN vs upstream error? We want to avoid marking these as gateway failures for both ops and billing.

jordan_infra: We can check socket state for FIN/FIN_WAIT close code and look at tcp close reason in the proxy. If kernel indicates remote close (RST/FIN) within 1s of write, classify as client_abort. Also can check whether any body bytes were delivered.

customer_acme: For billing we really need those to be client-abort (not bill as 5xx). Any ETA on a fix? This is customer-facing.

kevin_billing: From billing side — current rule: all 5xx label => not refundable. If we reclassify these to client_abort we can credit affected invoices. Need concrete list of request IDs and token counts to calculate credits.

alex_support: I'll gather token counts per request. Jordan, can you prototype heuristic and a short-term mitigation? E.g., treat EPIPE with source IP matching client as client abort instead of 5xx for now?

jordan_infra: I'll add a quick rule in the gateway: if write fails with EPIPE/EINTR and there was a preceding FIN from client within 2s, emit client_abort event and do not escalate to 5xx. Will roll a canary to staging in ~2 hours.

ingress-bot: deploy start: infra/proxy fix - canary to staging at 19:20Z (build a7c9f3).

maya_oncall: FYI also seeing a few chunked-trailer parsing errors (malformed chunk-size) in same window — could be buggy client libs sending unfinished chunk frames before closing. We'll flag that too.

customer_acme: Good catch — we can audit our client SDK. Quick question: in the curl repro above, is it sufficient to kill the process or do we need to half-close the connection? In our case the app calls socket.close() after receiving first token.

jordan_infra: Either approach triggers EPIPE. For repro, do: open streaming curl then `kill -9` the client process to emulate abrupt client close; or `printf "" > /proc/$PID/fd/3` to half-close. Both produce same symptom.

alex_support: Action items:
- alex_support: collect token counts and request IDs (submitted to billing)
- jordan_infra: prototype heuristic, canary to staging, monitor false positives
- maya_oncall: add alerts on chunked-parser errors and correlate with client IPs
- kevin_billing: prepare credit calc template once we hand over IDs

kevin_billing: If you drop the list in #billing-escalations I'll start calculations. We should also confirm the window for credits (we usually do 30 days retrospective).

customer_acme: Dropped a sample of 25 request IDs and token counts in a DM to alex_support. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :pray:

ingress-bot: deploy success: infra/proxy fix - canary to staging completed (a7c9f3) - monitor at https://ops.redwood.ai/canaries/a7c9f3

jordan_infra: Canary looks clean so far (30m). False-positive rate appears low in staging. I'll prepare a small prod rollout with safety kill switch.

maya_oncall: After prod rollout let's run a retrospective on classification thresholds; also add test coverage for chunked-abort paths in our e2e suite.

alex_support: Thanks all. Keeping thread open until prod rollout. Will update billing once I have IDs and token counts. :thumbsup:
